result:
PR #438 is ready for review. CI is green on 1d99bcb5d9 (both builds and the jobs selftest), and `preflight.sh --allow-tracker` passes.

**Why attempt 1 didn't finish:** the host stopped it to deliver the addendum. The work was uncommitted, the full selftest had been cut off, and the new tests had never been run against the old board.sh. When I did run them, they had two faults, fixed below. This is recorded in `docs/lanes/pri432/NOTES.md`.

**What's done:**
- **Dispatch order (1):** in board.sh's capacity list, every open `0.5` issue now comes before every other issue, and its line is tagged `[0.5]`. The existing ordering still applies within each group. An issue whose labels can't be read is still listed, tagged `[labels unreadable]`, and never counted as 0.5. roles/board.md's order paragraph says so.
- **Release focus (4):** setting `BOARD_FOCUS_LABEL` in `$WORK/limits.env` means only issues with that label are offered. One line, `N startable issue(s) outside the 0.5 focus are not offered`, goes to the tick log and the brief, but not into the list itself. Unset, behaviour is unchanged. The host still needs to set `BOARD_FOCUS_LABEL=0.5` once this folds.
- **Tests for 1 and 4:** the 13 new checks in 97-board-priority all pass on the new board.sh and all fail on master's; the 12 existing checks pass on both. Two faults in attempt 1's checks:
  - One check's pattern rejected the correct order.
  - The malformed-label test issue crashed the old board.sh. The other checks then "failed on old" only because nothing was printed, and one of them passed on old for the same reason. That issue now has its own test data.
- **Queue priority (2):** request.sh isn't in this lane's files, so this is written up in NOTES and filed as a board request (`board-requests/pri432.md`). The dispatcher serves requests in file-name order. The change is at `request.sh:701`: `ID="${HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO:+1-}$(date +%s)-$WHO-$$"`. A `1-` name sorts after the `0-*` probes and before every normal request; I checked the sort order on this host. The callers that would set the variable (ab_run.sh, arms.sh) are a second change, also outside this lane.
- **Status panel (3):** a new 0.5 box on the status page. It shows titles on the handhelds (23 of 145, plus 23 staged on the host), tested (0), Playable (0), the Ghoulies gate, and the lane on each 0.5 issue. The rendered text is pasted in NOTES.
  - Nothing records a staged ISO actually reaching a handheld (#430), so the panel says so rather than counting them as copied.
  - The gate medians (29 on the Thor, n=69; 29 on the Nova, n=71) match `fix311/read_soak.py` on the same runs. They come from a lane build, not a release candidate, so the panel says "met on these soaks (check the ref is the candidate's)" rather than "MET".

**Decision for you:** the v0.4.1-j1 candidate's Ghoulies soaks log no `hakuX-perf` lines at all, so the gate can't be read from them. The panel skips them and says how many it skipped. If the gate is meant to be read on a release build, that build has to log `hakuX-perf`.

**Unplanned fix:** the first CI run failed one check in `64-status-html.sh`, and master's own code fails it too. That fragment was reading the live `origin/board`, which CI also fetches. With today's board, the extra alerts pushed the check's expected line off the page. I pinned its runs to an empty board, added panel tests there, and added the file to the PR's Files line (no other open PR held it).

A full local selftest run also fails one other check, "a stale failure ALONGSIDE a live one is a live red" (fragment 76 or 87). It passes in CI and doesn't touch these files.
